newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Suharto warns about unchecked growth.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Suharto warns about unchecked growth.

text.p: Indonesian President Suharto on Monday warned about the dangers of urban growth in increasingly prosperous Asian cities.

"It is becoming more important to discuss the management of the growth of Asia's cities in a concerted and integrated manner," Suharto said at the opening of The Future of Asia's Cities, a seminar organised by the New York-based Asia Society and Indonesia's Centre for Information and Development Studies.
Suharto said problems facing Asian cities included pollution, a diminishing area of land available for agriculture and the emergence of a poverty-stricken urban class.

Cities in Indonesia accounted for 30 percent of the country's population in 1990, Suharto said. By 2015, 155 million people, or around 60 percent of Indonesians, were expected to live in urban centres, he added.
"This is the reason there is no other alternative but to pay serious attention so that the growth of cities is under control," Suharto said.
The United Nations says by the year 2025, the world's urban dwellers are expected to number around five billion. Eighty percent of them will live in developing countries.
